questions.question: Two identical metal spheres A and B carry charges +Q and −3Q respectively. They are brought into contact and then separated to their original distance. The ratio of the new force to the old force is:
questions.explanation: Initially, the force between the charges is: F = k(Q)(3Q) / r² = 3kQ² / r² After contact, total charge = +Q − 3Q = −2Q Since the spheres are identical, each sphere gets: −2Q / 2 = −Q New force: F′ = k(Q²) / r² Therefore, F′ / F = (kQ² / r²) ÷ (3kQ² / r²) = 1/3

questions.question: The value of the Coulomb constant k depends upon:

options.C: The system of units and the intervening medium

questions.explanation: Coulomb’s constant is: k = 1 / (4π ε₀ εᵣ) Therefore, it depends on the system of units and the medium between the charges.

questions.question: A point charge +q is placed at the center of a hollow conducting sphere. The electric field intensity at a point r (where r is less than the radius of sphere) is:
questions.explanation: Inside the hollow conducting sphere, the field due to the conducting shell is zero. Only the point charge contributes. Therefore, E = kq / r²

questions.question: If the electric flux through a closed surface is zero, then:

questions.explanation: According to Gauss’s Law: Φ = q enclosed / ε₀ If electric flux is zero, then enclosed charge must also be zero.

questions.question: A proton and an electron are placed in a uniform electric field. The ratio of their accelerations ap/ae will be:
questions.explanation: Force on each particle: F = qE Acceleration: a = F / m = qE / m Thus, ap / ae = me / mp because proton mass is much greater than electron mass.
